key_insight: Symbolic regression on limited inviscid surface data and viscous-flow skin-friction labels discovered an interpretable formula chain that predicts skin friction for attached flows across subsonic to hypersonic regimes.
engineering_relevance: The resulting analytical model offers a fast, physics-consistent alternative to costly CFD-based skin-friction estimation for aerodynamic design and drag prediction.
method: Use Euler surface-solution features together with viscous-flow skin-friction data.
Apply symbolic regression progressively to discover a unified analytical formula chain.
Add physically meaningful correction terms for pressure variation and Mach-number effects.
evidence_signal: The model was validated on typical geometries and reported low average integrated skin-friction drag prediction error with good generalization across freestream conditions and shapes.
watch_item: Performance is limited to attached-flow cases and depends on the representativeness of the training data for different Mach-number regimes and geometries.
paper_title: Skin friction prediction for attached flows based on two-dimensional inviscid solutions
